title: RBI Mandates Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR) for Derivative Contracts
content:
# RBI Mandates Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR) for Derivative Contracts

Ek important update hai Authorized Dealers (ADs) ke liye! The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) ne foreign exchange derivative contracts ke liye ek naya Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR) maintain karna mandatory kar diya hai, jo ki market ke orderly functioning ko ensure karega.

Yeh naye directions A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 26, dated October 10, 2026, ke through announce kiye gaye hain.

**Key Details:**

*   **What is FERR?** Authorised Dealers ko ab ek Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR) maintain karna hoga.
*   **Applicability:** Yeh mandate un foreign exchange derivative contracts par lagu hoga jo Indian Rupee (INR) involve karte hain aur jinki notional value USD two million equivalent se zyada hai.
*   **Purpose:** Specifically, yeh un contracts ke liye hai jo current account transactions ko hedge karne ke liye kiye jaate hain, jahan user foreign currency purchase kar raha hai against INR.
*   **Reserve Requirement:** ADs ko har eligible derivative contract ke notional amount ke INR equivalent ka 20% cash mein RBI ke paas deposit aur maintain karna hoga.
*   **Maintenance:** Yeh reserve daily basis par maintain kiya jayega aur contract ke termination tak rahega.
*   **Effective Date:** Yeh directions un foreign exchange derivative contracts par lagu honge jo is circular ke issue hone ke baad undertake kiye jayenge.
*   **Circumvention:** RBI ne yeh bhi kaha hai ki multiple transactions ke through is requirement ko circumvent karne ki koi bhi koshish violation mani jayegi.
